messages:
alex: Quick one - vendor call recap pasted below. We need a single ask list to close EDP: guaranteed usable GPU-hours mapping, ability to convert unused committed hours to burst credits, and an auditable metering SKU. Thoughts?
mina: +1 on SKU level metering. last month invoice line "GPU_COMMIT_A100" masked actual instance hour usage, made reconciliation painful.
luke: For Dedicated pools we need hard reservation on instance family + a 48h regional failover window. Can't have customers go down during region maintenance.
samir: AWS rep said they won't give hard failover unless we buy cross-region redundancy credits. Need numbers to compare vs our risk.
jane (aws-sales): @alex thanks - we can offer a cross-region standby guarantee for an additional 15% of committed spend, which converts to reserved capacity in another region during outages for up to 7 days/month.
tony (aws-contracts): Draft language proposal: "Provider shall maintain capacity equivalent to 95% of committed GPU-hours in the primary region; for outages >4h, provider will route to standby region and apply standby credits." We can make standby credits redeemable against committed spend.
alex: Concern: 15% hit feels steep. We expect normal failover <1% but want guardrails. Can we instead ask for a smaller percentage + SLA credits if they fail to deliver?
jane (aws-sales): We can do 8% standby if you accept a 2-year commit and a quarterly reconciliation clause.
mina: Reconciliation clause must include raw SKU-level hourly CSV export. Without that we can't map blended invoice dollars to actual GPU-hours consumed.
luke: Also require preemption transparency - if they use spare preemptible fleets to fulfill standby, it needs to be labeled as PREEMPTIBLE and not count toward guaranteed latency SLAs.
samir: tagging note: ensure NodePool mapping docs link in contract: which dedicated node types map to EDP SKUs, and how autoscaling interactions are billed.
jane (aws-sales): We can add a metering export: hourly rows with fields [timestamp, region, sku, instance_type, non_preemptible_hours, preemptible_hours, account_id].
mina: Perfect. Next: unused committed hours conversion. We want ability to convert up to 30% of unused monthly committed GPU-hours into burst credits that apply to on-demand pools in other regions. How flexible is that?
tony (aws-contracts): Legal: convertible credits can be allowed but must expire after 12 months and cannot be resold. We can add an escrow-style rollover for up to 3 months before expiration.
alex: Acceptable if expiry 12 months and 3 month escrow, but need explicit invoice lines for conversions and a daily balance report.
billing-bot: automated note: Example billing CSV row -> "1935000000,us-west-2,GPU-A100,instance.a100.40,nonpreemptible,12.0"
luke: Also pushing for an audit right: quarterly 3rd-party audit to validate metering. This is non-negotiable for finance.
tony (aws-contracts): Audit clause: mutually agreed auditor, one audit/year for material disputes, costs split if dispute validated.
mina: For preemptible vs non-preemptible discounts: need a clear rebate formula. If vendor serves >10% of hours as preemptible against committed non-preemptible hours, rebate applies.
jane (aws-sales): We can draft a "preemption rebate": if >10% of committed nonpreemptible hours are served as preemptible in a quarter, 50% of the difference refunded as credits.
alex: OK add that. Also ask for emergency capacity ramp timeline: vendor must provide >75% of ramped capacity within 6 hours of notification for critical incidents.
samir: Ops note: include specific API call they must support for capacity claim with response codes, e.g., POST /capacity/claim {region, gpu_family, hours_needed} -> 200/202 with iso timestamp.
jane (aws-sales): We can support an API contract for capacity claims; will need SOW.
luke: Final technical request: mapping for reserved pool vs on-demand eviction policies, plus a test window (one 8h failover drill per quarter) where vendor proves cross-region standby routing without counting against monthly usage.
alex: Great. Action items: 1) @jane & @tony to produce redlined contract with: standby percentage options (8% / 15%), SKU-level export, conversion rules (30% conversion, 12mo expiry, 3mo escrow), audit clause, preemption rebate, capacity claim API, emergency ramp 6h SLA, quarterly drill. 2) Finance (mina) to run cost model vs current baseline. 3) Eng (luke/samir) to draft NodePool mapping + test plan.
jane (aws-sales): I'll aim to share a first redline by EOD Wednesday.
mina: I'll have numbers by Friday afternoon.
samir: I'll sketch the NodePool mapping tomorrow.
luke: I'll draft failover drill runbook and metrics to validate.
alex: Thanks all - flagging legal for review after we get redline. :thumbsup:
